name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. This keeps contrast violations visible in real time, not just at review. The trade-off is a small runtime cost for every build, but it prevents costly fixes later. It matches our goal of speed and clarity by making contrast issues immediate and undeniable.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A live checker trains us to ignore warnings like a car’s seatbelt alarm—we learn to dismiss them. Instead, pre-submit gates force a deliberate pause, making contrast a non-negotiable rule, not a background noise. Settle it with a controlled test: run both for a week, measure ignored warnings vs. fixed violations, and let the data decide.

name: Facet
text:
Ship the pre-submission gate that blocks builds with insufficient contrast. This forces contrast to be treated as a hard rule, not a background noise, ensuring every release meets visibility standards. The trade-off is a slower release cycle for some builds, but it prevents costly fixes after launch and aligns with our goal of clarity and quality. A live checker alone risks warnings becoming noise—this gate makes contrast non-negotiable.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A pre-submit gate turns contrast into a gatekeeper’s whim—designers will game the metric or bypass it when deadlines loom. Instead, embed contrast checks in the live preview so violations flash red *while they work*, not just before they ship. Settle it with a two-week A/B test: track how often teams override gates versus how often they fix contrast *before* it becomes a problem.
